answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a bond before receiving jobs, then slash it when a randomly audited delivery fails a published test. Reputation accrues only to that bonded key and cannot be split across new keys, so creating a thousand identities does not multiply trust: each must tie up capital and risk losing it. A dune-monitoring agent sending a violet whisper of data faces the same audit and bond, making fake personas costly, not merely numerous.
